response.sql:
WITH kept AS (
  SELECT r.name AS raceName, ds.points AS pts
  FROM driverStandings ds
  JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId
  WHERE ds.points > 1.0
),
per_name AS (
  SELECT raceName, AVG(pts) AS avgPts
  FROM kept
  GROUP BY raceName
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avgPts) AS overallAvg FROM per_name
)
SELECT p.raceName AS raceName,
       p.avgPts AS avgPoints,
       p.avgPts - o.overallAvg AS differenceFromOverall
FROM per_name p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE p.avgPts > o.overallAvg
ORDER BY p.raceName;

assumptions.assumption: Race names are grouped by races.name alone, so same-named races from different seasons (for example every 'Australian Grand Prix' row) are pooled into one group.

driverStandings.points is used as stored. It is the season-to-date total the verified notes describe, so no per-race recomputation is done. Null points and standings with no matching race drop out through the WHERE clause and the inner JOIN.
Rows with a NULL races.name are not excluded and would form their own group. I did not check the data for NULL names.

alternatives.interpretation: "Clear" is read as "at least" 1.0, so entries with exactly 1.0 points are kept.
